nodes.label: Multi-Agent Architecture Patterns
nodes.rationale: Specialist multi-agent systems outperform single agents on PM tasks when roles match task specialisation. Evidence: MASAI (28.33% SWE-bench), MetaGPT, Orchestrating Human-AI Teams. PUMA Stage 5 SmartPMO multi-agent design.

nodes.label: Evaluation Metrics — Comprehensive Reference for PUMA
nodes.rationale: Catalogs all metrics for PUMA H1/H2: classification (F1-macro/micro/weighted, AUC-ROC), regression (MAE, MdAE, RMSE, SA, Spearman ρ), statistical (Wilcoxon, Cohen's d, bootstrap CI), LLM (ROUGE, BLEU, Recall@k, MRR), agent operational (SPR, latency), sustainability (CO2eq).

nodes.label: PUMA within Agentic Science Trajectory

nodes.label: The Uniqueness Trap — Why PM Estimation Fails and How PUMA Fixes It
nodes.rationale: Flyvbjerg's Uniqueness Trap: PMs treat each project as unique, discarding historical data. PUMA few-shot estimation = automated Reference Class Forecasting. Inside vs outside view. Planning fallacy, Kahneman, Taleb connections.

nodes.label: LLM Models Used in PUMA — Technical Reference

nodes.label: Computational Sustainability — Carbon Footprint of LLM Experiments
nodes.rationale: LLM inference carbon cost tracking via CodeCarbon. CO2eq = E × CI × PUE formula. Local vs cloud comparison: local Llama 3.2 8B ~24 gCO2eq vs GPT-4o ~1300 gCO2eq for 500 issues. Spain grid CI = 0.17 kg/kWh.

nodes.label: Agentic Science Paradigm

nodes.label: Statistical Validation — Wilcoxon, Bootstrap, Effect Size, and CI

nodes.label: PUMA Tool Selection Hierarchy

nodes.description: Cognitive bias where project managers resist using historical data from past projects by perceiving their current project as unique, causing systematic forecast errors.

nodes.label: Angermeir et al. 2025 — Reproducibility of LLM Studies in SE
nodes.description: Systematic mapping of 85 LLM-SE papers (2020–2024) showing only 5/18 artefacts are executable and zero are fully reproducible end-to-end.

nodes.label: Reproducibility Failure Taxonomy
nodes.description: Four-category taxonomy of why LLM-SE artefacts fail to reproduce: missing dependencies, undocumented preprocessing, non-deterministic API calls, and absent random seeds.

nodes.label: Spichkova/Cinkusz 2025 — Cognitive Agents for Agile PM
nodes.description: Empirical evaluation of LLM agents on five Agile PM tasks using GPT-4, showing CoT helps for structured tasks but lacking reproducibility, systematic prompting comparison, and carbon measurement.

nodes.label: Five Agile PM Tasks
nodes.description: The five project management tasks evaluated: story point estimation, issue triage, sprint planning, risk identification, and status reporting.

nodes.label: Axelos 2019 — ITIL Foundation ITIL 4
nodes.description: The global standard for IT service management defining the Service Value System, Service Value Chain, and 34 practices including Incident Management with SLA-based triage.

nodes.label: ITIL 4 Service Value Chain
nodes.description: ITIL 4's six-activity operational model (Plan, Improve, Engage, Design&Transition, Obtain/Build, Deliver&Support) providing the framework for SmartPMO operations.

nodes.label: ITIL Incident Management
nodes.description: ITIL practice for classifying and resolving unplanned service interruptions by priority (Critical/High/Medium/Low) with SLA time targets, directly mapped to PUMA's triage task.

nodes.label: MTTD and MTTR Metrics
nodes.description: Mean Time To Detect and Mean Time To Resolve, standard ITIL Incident Management KPIs used in PUMA's Stage 5 evaluation metrics.

nodes.label: PMI 2021 — PMBOK Guide 7th Edition
nodes.description: PMI's principles-based project management standard with 12 principles and 8 performance domains, replacing PMBOK 6's prescriptive process groups.

nodes.label: Value Delivery System (PMBOK 7)
nodes.description: PMBOK 7's framing of all PM functions as a portfolio of interconnected projects designed to deliver strategic outcomes, positioning SmartPMO as an automated value delivery layer.

nodes.label: 12 PM Principles (PMBOK 7)
nodes.description: Behaviour-focused principles replacing PMBOK 6 process groups, with Principles 4 (Value), 8 (Quality), 11 (Adaptability) most relevant to AI agent deployment.

nodes.label: Flyvbjerg 2023 — The Uniqueness Trap
nodes.description: Theoretical critique arguing that project managers systematically treat each project as unique, preventing statistical learning from historical data and causing systematic cost overruns.

nodes.label: Reference Class Forecasting
nodes.description: Evidence-based forecasting method that selects a reference class of similar past projects and uses their statistical distribution to anchor current project predictions.

nodes.label: Planning Fallacy
nodes.description: Kahneman & Tversky's cognitive bias describing the individual-level tendency to underestimate task duration and cost, which Flyvbjerg extends to organisational PM culture.

nodes.label: LLM-MAS-SE 2024 — LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems for SE
nodes.description: Vision paper providing a taxonomy of LLM-based MAS roles for SE and a challenge inventory (hallucination, coordination overhead, evaluation gap, reproducibility) with a research agenda.

nodes.label: MAS Roles Taxonomy for SE
nodes.description: Classification of LLM-based multi-agent system roles in software engineering: Requirements, Design, Developer, Tester, PM, and Reviewer agents.

nodes.label: PM-MAS Evaluation Gap
nodes.description: The absence of a standard benchmark for PM-specific MAS tasks (triage, estimation) that PUMA directly fills.

nodes.label: Shao et al. 2025 — Future of Work with AI Agents
nodes.description: Large-scale empirical study using the WORKBank database finding that ~40% of project manager tasks are automatable with current AI, with augmentation more likely than full substitution.

nodes.label: WORKBank Database
nodes.description: Database mapping O*NET occupational tasks to AI automation potential, used to quantify the ~40% automation estimate for project manager roles.

nodes.label: Cinkusz et al. 2025 — Cognitive Agents Powered by LLMs for Agile PM
nodes.description: Direct predecessor to PUMA evaluating LLM agents on five Agile PM tasks with GPT-4, lacking reproducibility, systematic prompting strategy comparison, and environmental measurement.

nodes.label: PUMA's Three Differentiating Gaps
nodes.description: The three limitations of Cinkusz et al. that PUMA addresses: lack of reproducibility (local models vs. API), no systematic prompting comparison (4 strategies), and no carbon measurement.

nodes.label: Assalaarachchi et al. 2026 — Toward Agentic SPM
nodes.description: First vision paper explicitly proposing 'Agentic Project Manager' as a research direction, with a three-level autonomy taxonomy and roadmap for Software Project Management 3.0.

nodes.label: APM Autonomy Levels
nodes.description: Three-level taxonomy for agentic project managers: Assistant (AI suggests), Co-pilot (AI leads), and Junior PM Agent (AI executes autonomously), mapping to PUMA Stages 1–5.

nodes.label: Software Project Management 3.0
nodes.description: Vision of autonomous AI agents taking over routine PM tasks while humans transition to strategic coaching roles.

nodes.label: Collaborating with AI Agents 2025 — Field Experiments
nodes.description: Field experiments measuring real-world effects of AI agent collaboration on team productivity and performance, providing ecological validity for augmentation vs. substitution debate.

nodes.label: AI Augmentation vs. Substitution
nodes.description: The distinction between AI that enhances human performance (augmentation) versus AI that replaces human workers (substitution), central to PUMA's ethics chapter.

nodes.label: Hevner et al. 2004 — Design Science in IS Research
nodes.description: Foundational paper establishing Design Science Research as a rigorous academic paradigm, providing seven guidelines, the three-cycle model, and an artefact taxonomy for IS research.

nodes.label: Seven DSR Guidelines
nodes.description: Hevner's seven guidelines for Design Science Research: Design as Artefact, Problem Relevance, Design Evaluation, Research Contributions, Research Rigour, Design as Search, and Communication.

nodes.label: DSR Artefact Taxonomy
nodes.description: Four types of DSR artefacts: Constructs (vocabulary), Models (abstractions), Methods (algorithms), and Instantiations (working implementations); PUMA is classified as an Instantiation.

nodes.label: Three DSR Research Cycles
nodes.description: Hevner's three interconnected cycles: Relevance (business problem grounding), Design (iterative build-evaluate), and Rigour (connection to knowledge base).

nodes.label: Kitchenham & Charters 2007 — SLR Guidelines for SE
nodes.description: The most widely cited systematic literature review guideline in software engineering, defining three phases (Planning, Conducting, Reporting) and the PICO framework for research questions.

nodes.label: PICO Framework
nodes.description: Research question formulation framework: Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome; used in PUMA's SLR to structure literature searches.

nodes.label: Three SLR Phases (Kitchenham)
nodes.description: Kitchenham's structured SLR process: Phase 1 Planning (protocol definition), Phase 2 Conducting (search, screening, extraction), Phase 3 Reporting (synthesis, PRISMA flow).

nodes.label: Page et al. 2021 — PRISMA 2020 Statement
nodes.description: Updated reporting guideline for systematic reviews with a 27-item checklist and flow diagram, explicitly addressing AI-assisted screening transparency.

nodes.label: PRISMA 2020 Flow Diagram
nodes.description: Standardised diagram tracking records through Identification, Screening, and Inclusion phases with explicit separation of database vs. register sources.

nodes.label: PRISMA-trAIce Protocol
nodes.description: PUMA's extension of PRISMA 2020 adding AI-transparency fields (AI tool, model version, validation date) for documenting AI-assisted screening decisions.

nodes.label: Li & Xu 2018 — Multi-Agent System for Distributed Multi-Project Scheduling
nodes.description: Multi-agent system using two-stage decomposition (local project agents + global coordinator) for distributed multi-project scheduling with negotiation-based resource conflict resolution.

nodes.label: Two-Stage MAS Decomposition
nodes.description: Architecture pattern where local project agents handle their own backlogs and a global coordinator resolves cross-project resource conflicts, mapping to PUMA Stage 5 SmartPMO.

nodes.label: Jumper et al. 2021 — AlphaFold2
nodes.description: AlphaFold2 predicts protein 3D structures with near-experimental accuracy using transformer-based attention over evolutionary sequence alignments, winning CASP14 by a large margin.

nodes.label: AI as Scientific Model (Level 2)
nodes.description: The LeCun framework level where AI learns implicit domain knowledge from data to solve prediction tasks previously requiring human expertise, analogous to PUMA's triage agent.

nodes.label: Degrave et al. 2022 — Plasma Control with Deep RL
nodes.description: Deep RL agent learns tokamak plasma control policies in simulation and transfers to the real TCV tokamak, discovering novel plasma configurations not achievable by classical controllers.

nodes.label: AI-Discovered Novel Strategies
nodes.description: RL agent discovering plasma configurations not anticipated by domain experts, constituting genuinely new operational knowledge beyond interpolation of training data.

nodes.label: Strubell et al. 2019 — Energy and Policy Considerations for Deep Learning in NLP
nodes.description: First systematic measurement of environmental cost of NLP model training, quantifying CO₂ equivalents for BERT and NAS models and recommending reporting standards.

nodes.label: CO₂ Measurement Methodology for ML
nodes.description: Two-factor model CO₂eq = Energy × Carbon Intensity, extended by CodeCarbon with PUE, forming the methodological basis for PUMA's sustainability measurement.

nodes.label: CodeCarbon
nodes.description: Software tool implementing Strubell et al.'s CO₂ measurement methodology with PUE extension, integrated into PUMA experiments as a first-class environmental variable.

nodes.label: Jain et al. 2023 — GNoME Materials Discovery
nodes.description: GNoME uses graph neural network with active learning to discover 2.2 million stable crystal structures, expanding known stable materials ~10× through AI-driven materials science.

nodes.label: Active Learning for Scientific Discovery
nodes.description: Iterative cycle of GNN prediction → DFT verification → retraining enabling scalable discovery of stable crystal structures beyond what humans could achieve manually.

nodes.label: Arkani-Hamed et al. 2026 — Gluon Amplitudes (GPT-5.2)
nodes.description: GPT-5.2 Pro derives closed-form expressions for single-minus gluon tree amplitudes previously assumed zero, correcting an established belief in theoretical physics.

nodes.label: LLM Correcting Established Expert Beliefs
nodes.description: One of the first documented cases of an LLM correcting an established scientific belief, demonstrating that LLMs can exceed pattern-matching interpolation at the knowledge frontier.

nodes.label: Lam et al. 2023 — GraphCast Weather Forecasting
nodes.description: GraphCast GNN outperforms ECMWF's HRES in >90% of 1380 metrics for 10-day global weather forecasting at orders of magnitude lower computational cost.

nodes.label: AI Surpassing Rule-Based Baseline (GraphCast)
nodes.description: Pattern where a learned AI model replaces a classical/rule-based system and achieves measurably superior performance on defined evaluation metrics, analogous to PUMA triage agent vs. majority-class baseline.

nodes.label: Lu et al. 2024 — The AI Scientist
nodes.description: Fully automated pipeline for end-to-end ML research (ideation → coding → experiments → writing → review) producing papers at workshop acceptance quality.

nodes.label: AI Scientist Four-Stage Research Pipeline
nodes.description: Ideation → Execution → Analysis → Communication pipeline for automated research, directly mappable to PUMA SmartPMO: triage → estimation → risk detection → reporting.

nodes.label: Klinger et al. 2025 — AI for Scientific Discovery is a Social Problem
nodes.description: Position paper arguing that AI's impact on scientific discovery depends on socio-institutional structures (open data, reproducibility, attribution, governance) as much as on technical advances.

nodes.label: AI Science Governance Requirements
nodes.description: Four institutional requirements for responsible AI-generated research: open data infrastructure, mandatory reproducibility, attribution frameworks, and governance structures.

nodes.label: PUMA Project
nodes.description: Project Understanding and Management with Agents — a reproducible benchmark for LLM agents on PM triage and story point estimation tasks using local open-source models.

nodes.label: SmartPMO
nodes.description: PUMA's Stage 5 vision of a fully automated Project Management Office integrating triage, estimation, and routing agents under human oversight.

nodes.label: Human-in-the-Loop (HITL)
nodes.description: Design principle where AI agents suggest or lead but humans retain decision authority, central to PUMA's responsible AI deployment and ethics framework.

nodes.label: HAIF Framework
nodes.description: Human-AI Integration Framework defining roles, responsibilities, authority levels, governance models, and escalation protocols for hybrid human-AI teams.

nodes.label: Li et al. (2026) HAIF
nodes.description: Paper proposing HAIF, a governance framework for hybrid human-AI team operations with bounded agent autonomy.

nodes.label: Human-in-the-Loop (HITL)
nodes.description: Design principle requiring human approval for agent decisions at critical checkpoints to ensure safe agentic operation.

nodes.label: Agent Governance Model
nodes.description: Model defining which decisions agents can make autonomously and which require human approval, with escalation paths on failure.

nodes.label: Gao et al. (2023) AssistGUI
nodes.description: Paper proposing AssistGUI, a system for task-oriented desktop GUI automation via LLMs with visual understanding.

nodes.label: GUI Automation Agent
nodes.description: Agent that perceives desktop UI elements visually and executes atomic actions (click, type, scroll) to complete natural language instructions.

nodes.label: AssistGUI Pipeline
nodes.description: Five-stage pipeline: task understanding, screen perception, action planning, execution, and verification with retry on failure.

nodes.label: Wang et al. (2024) OpenHands
nodes.description: Paper presenting OpenHands, an open-source platform for building AI software agents with sandboxed code execution and multi-agent coordination.

nodes.label: OpenHands Platform
nodes.description: MIT-licensed open-source platform (formerly OpenDevin) for generalist AI software developer agents with sandboxed execution and tool use.

nodes.label: Sandboxed Code Execution
nodes.description: Isolated execution environment for agent-generated code, preventing unintended side effects in production systems.

nodes.label: Chen et al. (2024) RCA
nodes.description: EuroSys 2024 paper on Microsoft's production LLM-based automated root cause analysis system for cloud incidents.

nodes.label: LLM Root Cause Analysis
nodes.description: Automated system using LLMs for multi-step reasoning over telemetry data to identify root causes of cloud incidents, deployed in Microsoft production.

nodes.label: AIOps Incident Triage
nodes.description: Automated operations using AI to triage and resolve IT incidents, reducing mean time to detect (MTTD) in production environments.

nodes.label: Chen et al. (2025) HiveMind
nodes.description: Paper proposing HiveMind, a framework for swarm-level optimization of LLM agent behaviors through collective intelligence.

nodes.label: Swarm-Level Agent Optimization
nodes.description: Optimization approach where collective interaction among swarm agents produces emergent collective intelligence surpassing individual agent optimization.

nodes.label: Masterman et al. (2024) Agent Arch Survey
nodes.description: Survey covering 30+ agent architectures with taxonomy of single vs. multi-agent, reasoning patterns, and tool integration patterns.

nodes.label: Agent Architecture Taxonomy
nodes.description: Classification of agent architectures from tool-augmented LLM to fully autonomous multi-agent, covering single vs. multi-agent and reasoning patterns.

nodes.label: Reasoning Patterns (CoT, ToT, ReAct, Reflexion)
nodes.description: Family of LLM reasoning techniques surveyed including Chain-of-Thought, Tree-of-Thoughts, ReAct, and Reflexion.

nodes.label: Jimenez et al. (2023) SWE-bench
nodes.description: ICLR 2024 paper proposing SWE-bench, a benchmark of 2294 real GitHub issues requiring code patches to evaluate LLM software engineering capabilities.

nodes.label: SWE-bench Dataset
nodes.description: Benchmark of 2294 real GitHub issues from 12 repositories, validated by test suites, for evaluating LLM code-fix capabilities.

nodes.label: Dorri et al. (2025) Orchestrating Human-AI
nodes.description: DAI 2025 paper positioning the Manager Agent as the central challenge in multi-agent systems and providing a competency framework.

nodes.label: Manager Agent
nodes.description: Orchestrator agent that decomposes goals, refines tasks, assigns them to sub-agents, and coordinates multi-agent team execution.

nodes.label: Proactive Orchestrator Pattern
nodes.description: Manager agent behavior pattern of decompose-refine-assign-get_agents, contrasted with reactive communicator (send_message-status_check).

nodes.label: Yu et al. (2025) DynTaskMAS
nodes.description: Paper proposing DynTaskMAS, a dynamic task graph framework enabling asynchronous and parallel LLM multi-agent execution.

nodes.label: Dynamic Task Graph
nodes.description: Task graph that updates dynamically as agent outputs arrive, enabling non-blocking parallel execution of independent sub-tasks.

nodes.label: Arora et al. (2024) MASAI
nodes.description: Microsoft Research paper proposing MASAI, a modular multi-agent architecture achieving 28.33% on SWE-bench Lite via specialist sub-agents.

nodes.label: MASAI Modular Sub-Agent Architecture
nodes.description: Architecture where each sub-agent has a narrow objective and specific tools, reducing error accumulation versus monolithic single-agent approaches.

nodes.label: Tao et al. (2024) MAGIS
nodes.description: Paper proposing MAGIS, an LLM multi-agent framework with manager, repository curator, developer, and QA roles for GitHub issue resolution.

nodes.label: MAGIS Role-Team Pattern
nodes.description: Multi-agent team pattern with Manager, Repository Curator, Developer, and QA agents, each with role-specific context retrieval.

nodes.label: Hu et al. (2024) GraphAgent
nodes.description: EMNLP 2025 paper proposing GraphAgent, a unified agentic LLM for graph-structured and text data using a plan-then-execute framework.

nodes.label: Agentic Graph-RAG
nodes.description: Plan-then-execute approach for querying and reasoning over knowledge graphs agentically, combining graph structure with LLM capabilities.

nodes.label: Tang et al. (2025) LLMOrbit
nodes.description: Survey paper presenting a circular taxonomy of LLMs from base scaling to instruction-tuned and agentic AI systems.

nodes.label: LLM Circular Taxonomy
nodes.description: Taxonomy of LLM evolution: base LLM → instruction tuning → RLHF → agentic capabilities, with the scaling wall concept marking diminishing returns.

nodes.label: Scaling Wall Concept
nodes.description: Phenomenon of diminishing returns from raw parameter scaling, motivating the shift to instruction tuning and agentic prompting strategies.

nodes.label: Hubinger et al. (2019) Learned Optimization
nodes.description: Foundational AI safety paper introducing mesa-optimization, inner alignment, and deceptive alignment risks in learned systems.

nodes.label: Mesa-Optimization
nodes.description: The phenomenon where a trained model internally performs its own optimization process, potentially diverging from the intended base objective.

nodes.label: Inner Alignment Problem
nodes.description: The problem where the mesa-optimizer's learned objective diverges from the base optimizer's intended objective, causing misaligned behavior.

nodes.label: Deceptive Alignment
nodes.description: Scenario where a mesa-optimizer behaves correctly during training/evaluation but pursues a different goal once deployed without oversight.

nodes.label: Zhang et al. (2024) Intelligent Spark Agents
nodes.description: Paper proposing a modular LangGraph framework for orchestrating Apache Spark ML workflows with visualized agent pipelines.

nodes.label: LangGraph Orchestration
nodes.description: Framework for modular agentic pipeline orchestration supporting cyclic workflows, used to coordinate agent execution steps.

nodes.label: Ning et al. (2024) Agent Taxonomy
nodes.description: Paper presenting a multi-dimensional taxonomy and decision model for selecting foundation model-based agent architectures.

nodes.label: Agent Architecture Decision Model
nodes.description: Decision framework for choosing agent architecture dimensions (single vs. multi-agent, reactive vs. deliberative, with/without memory) based on task requirements.

nodes.label: DeBellis et al. (2026) Authenticated Workflows
nodes.description: Paper proposing an authentication and authorization framework for multi-step agentic workflows with audit trail support.

nodes.label: Agentic Workflow Authentication
nodes.description: Systems-level model for authenticating agent actions and preventing unauthorized operations in agentic pipelines interacting with real APIs.

nodes.label: Park et al. (2023) Generative Agents
nodes.description: ACM UIST 2023 paper presenting 25 generative agents with memory streams, reflection, and planning in a social simulation environment.

nodes.label: Memory Stream Architecture
nodes.description: Timestamped event log with recency, importance, and relevance scoring for agent memory, enabling context-aware retrieval.

nodes.label: Agent Reflection Mechanism
nodes.description: Periodic synthesis of higher-level abstract insights from lower-level memory events, enabling agents to form generalized beliefs.

nodes.label: Agent Hierarchical Planning
nodes.description: Coarse daily plan decomposed into atomic 5–15 minute actions, maintaining time-consistency for long-horizon agent behavior.

nodes.label: Wang et al. (2025) Flow
nodes.description: Paper proposing Flow, a modular agentic workflow system where reusable agent components compose into explicit workflow graphs.

nodes.label: Modular Agentic Workflow
nodes.description: Architecture pattern composing reusable agent modules into explicit workflow graphs, improving generalization over monolithic pipelines.

nodes.label: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts
nodes.description: NeurIPS 2023 paper proposing Tree of Thoughts, extending CoT to tree-based search over reasoning steps with BFS/DFS/beam variants.

nodes.label: Tree of Thoughts (ToT)
nodes.description: Deliberate problem-solving method that explores multiple reasoning branches using tree search, evaluated by the LLM at each step.

nodes.label: Huang et al. (2024) Internet of Agents
nodes.description: EMNLP 2024 paper proposing Internet of Agents, a protocol for heterogeneous agent discovery and composition across providers.

nodes.label: Heterogeneous Agent Protocol
nodes.description: Internet-like routing and discovery protocol enabling agents from different providers, models, and frameworks to collaborate.

nodes.label: Hong et al. (2023) MetaGPT
nodes.description: ICLR 2024 paper proposing MetaGPT, a multi-agent framework encoding SOPs into role-specialised agents for software development.

nodes.label: MetaGPT Role-Based SOP
nodes.description: Structured workflow encoding real-world Standard Operating Procedures into multi-agent roles (PM, Architect, Engineer, QA) with artifact-driven communication.

nodes.label: Yao et al. (2022) ReAct
nodes.description: ICLR 2023 foundational paper proposing ReAct, which interleaves Thought-Action-Observation cycles to synergize reasoning and acting in LLMs.

nodes.label: ReAct Pattern
nodes.description: Agent interaction loop alternating Thought (internal reasoning), Action (tool call), and Observation (tool output) to ground decisions in retrieved evidence.

nodes.label: PUMA Smart PMO
nodes.description: PUMA Stage 5 multi-agent project management orchestrator handling triage, estimation, and planning across Jira and GitHub.

nodes.label: Real-World Task Benchmark Design
nodes.description: Benchmark methodology using real-world tasks with verified ground truth rather than synthetic data to expose true LLM capability gaps.

nodes.label: AutoGen
nodes.description: Microsoft's open-source multi-agent conversation framework supporting customizable roles, GroupChat abstraction, and human-in-the-loop checkpoints.

nodes.label: GroupChat abstraction
nodes.description: AutoGen's mechanism where multiple agents take turns contributing to a shared conversation managed by a GroupChatManager.

nodes.label: Human-in-the-Loop (HITL)
nodes.description: Design principle for inserting human approval checkpoints into multi-agent workflows.

nodes.label: Multi-Agent Collaboration Survey (Talebirad 2023)
nodes.description: Early survey of LLM-based multi-agent systems providing a taxonomy of architectures and communication patterns.

nodes.label: Multi-Agent Architecture Taxonomy
nodes.description: Classification of LLM multi-agent architectures including hierarchical, peer-to-peer, and broadcast communication patterns.

nodes.label: MemGPT
nodes.description: System treating LLMs as operating systems with virtual context management (main context + external storage) for persistent memory across conversations.

nodes.label: Virtual Context Management
nodes.description: OS-inspired approach using agent-controlled memory paging between active context and external storage to overcome LLM context window limits.

nodes.label: Quiet-STaR (Zelikman 2024)
nodes.description: Method for LLMs to generate internal rationales for every token during training, reinforcing rationales that improve predictions without supervised CoT examples.

nodes.label: Self-Training Chain-of-Thought
nodes.description: Unsupervised training methodology where LLMs learn to generate rationales that improve downstream predictions without labeled reasoning examples.

nodes.label: OpenAgents
nodes.description: Open platform with three specialized agents (Data Agent, Plugins Agent, Web Agent) for real-world deployable language agent applications.

nodes.label: Data Agent Pattern
nodes.description: Architecture pattern where NL queries are converted to Python/pandas code, executed in a sandbox, with errors fed back to the LLM for self-correction.

nodes.label: Chain-of-Thought Prompting
nodes.description: Prompting technique including intermediate reasoning steps that dramatically improves LLM performance on multi-step reasoning tasks.

nodes.label: Chain-of-Thought Paper (Wei 2022)
nodes.description: NeurIPS 2022 paper establishing CoT prompting as an emergent capability and documenting the scaling law for CoT effectiveness above ~100B parameters.

nodes.label: Zero-Shot CoT
nodes.description: Eliciting chain-of-thought reasoning by appending 'Let's think step by step' without examples, leveraging latent reasoning structure in large models.

nodes.label: AgentBench
nodes.description: First comprehensive benchmark for evaluating LLMs as agents across 8 distinct environments (OS, DB, KG, ALFWorld, WebShop, Mind2Web, House3D, Minecraft).

nodes.label: Open-Source vs GPT-4 Agent Gap
nodes.description: Empirical finding that open-source LLMs score only 5-30% of GPT-4 on agentic tasks due to format-following and long-context reasoning failures.

nodes.label: ChatDev
nodes.description: Multi-agent software development system using a chat-chain of sequential role-based communication (CEO, CTO, programmer, reviewer, tester).

nodes.label: Transformer Architecture
nodes.description: Neural network architecture based solely on attention mechanisms, eliminating recurrence and enabling parallelism that underlies all modern LLMs.

nodes.label: Attention Is All You Need (Vaswani 2017)
nodes.description: Foundational NeurIPS 2017 paper introducing the Transformer architecture with scaled dot-product attention and multi-head attention.

nodes.label: Multi-Head Attention
nodes.description: Mechanism running attention multiple times in parallel with different learned projections, enabling models to attend to different representation aspects simultaneously.

nodes.label: AgentScope
nodes.description: Alibaba's flexible multi-agent platform with actor-model concurrency, fault-tolerant pipelines, and multiple LLM backends including Ollama.

nodes.label: Actor-Model Concurrency
nodes.description: Concurrency pattern allowing parallel execution of multiple specialist agents, enabling simultaneous multi-agent processing of tasks.

nodes.label: Reflexion
nodes.description: Framework adding verbal reinforcement self-critique loops on top of ReAct, where agents generate natural language reflections on failures stored in episodic memory.

nodes.label: Verbal Reinforcement Learning
nodes.description: Using natural language critique as a richer gradient signal than numeric reward, allowing agents to improve without weight updates.

nodes.label: Episodic Memory (Reflexion)
nodes.description: Persisting verbal self-critiques across trials in a buffer included in subsequent prompts, enabling iterative agent improvement without retraining.

nodes.label: GAIA Benchmark
nodes.description: Benchmark of 466 real-world multi-step tasks across 3 difficulty levels evaluating general AI assistant capabilities.

nodes.label: Switch Transformers
nodes.description: JMLR 2022 paper introducing single-expert routing MoE to scale Transformers to trillion parameters with manageable compute.

nodes.label: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE)
nodes.description: Architecture routing each token to a subset of specialized expert networks, growing total parameters while keeping activated parameters per token constant.

nodes.label: Agentic Science Paradigm
nodes.description: Research paradigm where AI agents manage complete investigation cycles from hypothesis to conclusion with limited human oversight.

nodes.label: From AI for Science to Agentic Science Survey (Zhang 2025)
nodes.description: Survey on autonomous scientific discovery covering a three-phase framework from AI tools through collaborative AI to fully agentic science.

nodes.label: Three-Phase AI Science Framework
nodes.description: Progression from AI for Science (tool phase) through AI in Science (collaborative) to Agentic Science (autonomous full-cycle research).

nodes.label: Theory Is All You Need (Felin 2024)
nodes.description: Position paper arguing data-driven AI is fundamentally retrospective and cannot generate novel causal scientific theory unlike prospective human cognition.

nodes.label: AI Causal Reasoning Limits
nodes.description: Argument that AI cognition is retrospective and correlational while human cognition is prospective and causal, limiting AI's theory-generation capacity.

nodes.label: Emotions & Developer Productivity Survey (Weichbroth 2025)
nodes.description: Survey on emotional factors and burnout affecting software developer productivity, relevant to automation rationale for repetitive tasks.

nodes.label: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
nodes.description: Anthropic-introduced standard for tool integration between LLM agents and external services, enabling structured access to APIs and data sources.

nodes.label: MCP Security Survey (Hou 2025)
nodes.description: First academic survey of the MCP landscape with a security threat taxonomy covering injection attacks, tool poisoning, and data exfiltration.

nodes.label: MCP Security Threat Taxonomy
nodes.description: Classification of MCP security threats including prompt injection attacks, tool poisoning, and data exfiltration vectors.

nodes.label: AIOpsLab
nodes.description: Microsoft's holistic benchmark framework for evaluating AI agents on cloud operations covering detection, diagnosis, and mitigation with 30+ tasks.

nodes.label: Incident Management in the Age of AI Survey (2023)
nodes.description: Survey of AI/ML applications across the IT incident lifecycle (detection, triage, RCA, mitigation) including AI technique taxonomy and dataset catalog.

nodes.label: Incident Management Lifecycle
nodes.description: Structured lifecycle of IT incident handling phases: detection, triage, root cause analysis, mitigation, and post-incident review.

nodes.label: AIDOaRt Framework
nodes.description: EU H2020 AI-augmented automation framework for DevOps in cyber-physical systems covering requirements, testing, monitoring, and deployment phases.

nodes.label: MCP Protocol Video Collection
nodes.description: Curated collection of 28 videos covering MCP fundamentals, security, practical implementations, and browser automation for PUMA Stage 5 integration.

nodes.label: SLR + PRISMA Pipeline
nodes.description: Systematic literature review workflow following PRISMA methodology with AI-assisted screening for the PUMA research project.

nodes.label: PRISMA Methodology
nodes.description: Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses framework for structured, transparent literature review reporting.

nodes.label: Spec-Driven Development (SDD)
nodes.description: Software engineering paradigm using detailed specifications as the primary artifact driving agentic code generation and development.

nodes.label: Agentic Software Engineering
nodes.description: Emerging discipline where AI agents manage full software development workflows with structured autonomy and human oversight.

nodes.label: Context Engineering
nodes.description: Evolution beyond prompt engineering that systematically manages the full context window for reliable agentic AI behavior.

nodes.label: BIB-Supplement-AIKnowledge
nodes.description: Verified APA7 bibliography supplement covering AI and new scientific knowledge for Milestone 2, organized into 10 thematic sections.

nodes.label: AI Scientist (Lu et al. 2024/2026)
nodes.description: Fully automated open-ended scientific discovery system by Lu et al., with v2 introducing agentic tree search for workshop-level discovery.

nodes.label: Agentic Science Survey
nodes.description: Survey by Zhang et al. (2025) covering the transition from AI for science to autonomous agentic scientific discovery.

nodes.label: Gemini 2.5 Pro — IMO 2025 Gold
